h1: Are ADUs allowed in Massachusetts?
description: Massachusetts' 2024 Affordable Homes Act protects one accessory dwelling unit on single-family lots. What the law (M.G.L. c.40A §3) and state guidance say.

h1: Can a homeowner do electrical, plumbing or gas work in Newton, MA?
description: What Newton and Massachusetts say about who can pull electrical, plumbing and gas permits, which minor plumbing repairs need no permit, and water heater permits.

h1: How big can an ADU be in Massachusetts?
description: The Massachusetts ADU size cap: half the main home's gross floor area or 900 sq ft, whichever is smaller. Plus how floor area is counted, and Newton's local limits.

h1: How do I close an open permit in Newton, MA?
description: Old Newton permits do not close on their own. What the City says about closing them, who may call, and why to hold final payment until closure.

h1: How do I find my zoning district in Newton, MA?
description: Where to look up your Newton zoning district: the City's interactive zoning map and GIS Browser, and what the ordinance says about the Official Zoning Map.

h1: How do I get a building permit in Newton, MA?
description: Step-by-step: how Newton building permits are applied for online, what the City checklist asks for, how fees are calculated, and the inspections that follow.

h1: What are the ADU rules in Newton, MA?
description: Newton accessory dwelling unit rules from Ord. Sec. 6.7.1: one per lot, no extra parking, 30-day minimum rentals, and size limits for internal and detached ADUs.

h1: How tall can a house be in Newton, MA?
description: Newton's maximum house heights: 36 feet sloped roof, 30 feet flat roof, 2.5 stories (3 by special permit), and how height is measured.

h1: How do building inspections work in Newton, MA?
description: How to schedule a Newton building inspection, the call-before-8-AM rule, and what must be ready at each stage from excavation to final.

h1: What is Newton's demolition delay, and does it apply to my house?
description: Newton Historical Commission demolition review: buildings 50+ years old (including garages and sheds), partial demolition, 12- and 18-month delays, and waivers.

h1: Do new homes and renovations in Newton have to be all-electric?
description: Newton's Specialized Energy Code (since 2024) and fossil-fuel-free ordinance: electrified heating, cooling, cooking and drying for new builds and major renovations.

h1: What is the floor area ratio (FAR) limit in Newton, MA?
description: How Newton defines FAR, the maximum FAR by lot size for SR and MR districts (Ord. Sec. 3.1.9 and 3.2.11), and the City's FAR calculator.

h1: What needs approval in a Newton local historic district?
description: In a Newton local historic district, exterior changes, including hardscaping, need Historic District Commission review. How the certificates work.

h1: What is the maximum lot coverage in Newton, MA?
description: Newton's maximum lot coverage percentages for SR1–SR3 and MR1–MR4 from Ord. Sec. 3.1.3 and 3.2.3, by lot creation date.

h1: How do I apply for and track a permit on Newton's online portal?
description: How Newton's online permitting works: the OpenGov account, starting an application, public record search by address, and checking permits are closed.

h1: What are Newton's SR and MR zoning districts?
description: What Newton's Single Residence (SR1–SR3) and Multi-Residence (MR1–MR4) districts are and which housing types the ordinance allows in each.

h1: What is the difference between a special permit and a variance in Newton?
description: Who grants special permits and variances in Newton, the two-thirds City Council vote, site plan approval, and the legal tests for a variance.

h1: Do I need a permit to cut down a tree in Newton, MA?
description: Newton's Tree Preservation Ordinance (Ch. 21): which trees are protected (6 inches DBH and up), when a tree permit is needed, and replacement rules.

h1: What are the zoning setbacks in Newton, MA?
description: Newton's minimum front, side and rear setbacks for SR and MR districts from Ord. Sec. 3.1.3 and 3.2.3, including the December 7, 1953 lot-date split.

h1: Do I need a permit for solar panels in Newton, MA?
description: Newton's fee schedule lists building permits for solar panels, with and without structural work, plus a separate electrical permit for solar.
